International oil prices extended their pullback as Middle Eastern crude exports showed signs of recovery and market expectations grew for an easing of tensions between the United States and Iran. London Brent crude futures and US West Texas Intermediate crude futures fell 3.55% and 3.58% overnight, respectively. Over the past month, cumulative declines for both benchmark contracts have approached 16%.
In an interview with CNBC, analysts noted that while crude oil export volumes from the Persian Gulf have increased, the outflows consist primarily of unrefined crude, meaning supplies of refined products such as diesel have not improved in tandem. Meanwhile, with the Thanksgiving and Christmas holidays approaching, market liquidity is tightening, prompting many large hedge funds to take profits and hold cash on the sidelines. Under these conditions, oil prices are more vulnerable to short term news headlines and systematic algorithmic trading.
Furthermore, considering the appointment of Stephen Miller, who advocates a hardline policy toward Iran, as White House Chief of Staff, the United States recently deployed three aircraft carrier strike groups to the Middle East while launching Operation Iron Gate to tighten the blockade on Iran. Consequently, US policy toward Iran has not undergone any substantive shift, and Gulf states may need to prepare for a protracted conflict. Against this backdrop, any renewed escalation could drive oil prices higher once again.
AMRITA SEN 
Founder 
Energy Aspects
"I will say the market's extremely complacent. If Iran doesn't start to kind of give something, the risk of escalation is still there and still high."
However, once geopolitical tensions genuinely ease, pressure on oil producing nations to compete for market share could resurface.
To advance its economic diversification transition, the United Arab Emirates has sought to accelerate the monetization of its oil and gas resources, even exiting OPEC in May of this year to free itself from production quota constraints. If the US Iran conflict is resolved and a ceasefire is achieved between Russia and Ukraine, supplies from producers including the UAE, Iran, and Saudi Arabia are expected to rise. Combined with incremental output from the United States, Canada, and Brazil, the crude market would fall into a supply surplus, potentially triggering a sharp drop in oil prices.
FEREIDUN FESHARAKI 
Chairman Emeritus 
FGE NexantECA
"Our analysis indicates two and a half to 3 million barrels per day of surplus from the second half of 2027, and this would basically mean that either OPEC Plus has to cut volume, or the prices will go down to $60 a barrel."

articles.title: Analysis: The Fed's chairman sees an AI revolution coming. Now he has to figure out what it means
articles.text:
Artificial intelligence is about to sweep through the economy. The Federal Reserve is bracing for impact.
"We are at a hinge point in the U.S. economy," Fed Chairman Kevin Warsh said at a conference he convened in San Francisco on Monday. But exactly when and how the economy could turn, and what that means for interest rates and inflation, isn't yet clear.
The meeting of Warsh's AI task force saw the new Fed chairman publicly asking the questions Americans will ultimately expect him to answer. He hinted at a few of his private views on whether white-collar workers could soon face massive job losses, but he largely left the speculation to an array of experts he has assembled to advise the Fed.
With the technology racing ahead, Warsh won't be able to put off giving his own answers much longer. AI lab Anthropic plans to price the shares for its initial public offering on Wednesday and could raise as much as $64 billion at a $1.4 trillion valuation. Vast spending from AI firms is prompting the Fed to contemplate raising interest rates in December to slow down the rate of price increases as the tech sector heats up the economy.
Meanwhile Americans are souring on some aspects of the technology. The Nov. 3 midterms saw voters enact an array of state-level measures to slow down construction of the data centers that are essential to powering AI.
Warsh moderated three out of four sessions at Monday's event and was involved in selecting the speakers. Among them was one of the few prominent Democrats who was willing to speak out against that anti-data center trend.
It is "a very troubling sign" that so many anti-data center measures passed in the midterms, Gina Raimondo said. She is a former secretary of commerce under President Joe Biden and a former governor of Rhode Island.
Stopping AI "would be very bad for America" and for the people who voted for the measures, Raimondo said.
Warsh didn't say whether he shares that view, and how it would translate into monetary policy isn't exactly clear.
The event was an unusual one for the Fed. The central bank employs a small army of Ph.D. economists who can rapidly weigh in on anything affecting the U.S. and global economies. But in keeping with his longstanding critiques of the Fed as insular and outdated, Warsh has chosen to draw expertise from outside the institution to help it figure out how to think about what AI will do to productivity and jobs.
Warsh has assembled a task force on that issue, alongside four others devoted to aspects of Fed policymaking.
The public heard Monday from one of the three official members of the task force: venture capitalist Marc Andreessen. Warsh went to Stanford University with Andreessen's wife, and the two have been longtime friends. Another task force member, Stanford economist Chad Jones, is on leave and working at Anthropic and couldn't speak during the company's blackout period ahead of the IPO. The third, Xbox CEO Asha Sharma, didn't attend the event.
Andreessen is hugely optimistic about the promise of AI as a technology, but believes the government won't let Americans experience its full effects. Heavy regulation in areas such as healthcare and education mean technology can't replace people's jobs in those sectors, he said.
"To the extent our economy is a free-market economy, then maybe you could see the, let's say, extremely rapid displacement scenarios people are talking about," Andreessen said. "But we've mostly outlawed the kind of job transition that … both the utopians the doomers talk about."
Warsh returned repeatedly to one scenario for the economy that draws on past experience. The so-called China shock unfolded after that country joined the World Trade Organization in 2001 and moved heavily into low-cost manufacturing. Americans saw prices on clothing and furniture drop rapidly, for instance, but at the cost of severe job losses. One widely cited estimate found the U.S. lost a million manufacturing jobs and 2.4 million jobs overall in the years that followed.
Warsh suggested to one of the panelists that the widespread adoption of AI might produce its own version of the China shock, this time focused on service workers.
"I don't want to hold this too tightly," Warsh said. "But if in some ways over the last generation or generation and a half, the China shock, for lack of a better word, lowered prices of goods in the United States, the way that I heard you talking about the philosophy of this new technology is it might do something for services."
In other words, AI could do, say, legal or administrative work more cheaply than a human. That could lower prices but put many people out of a job.
Warsh asked panelists whether "we should expect disinflation over the medium term, from what AI could do to services."
They largely suggested it was possible, which could mean the Fed might eventually want to lower interest rates over the long term.
But at the end of the day, it is Warsh and his fellow Fed members who will need to have conviction on the answer.
There are still many steps between the task force discussion and any kind of change in Fed policy. First, the three task force members will have to assemble their points of view into a report for Warsh sometime in the next few months. Then the Fed itself will need to debate those results and decide whether or how to use them to shape monetary policy.
But with AI growing bigger every day, the Fed may need to make up its mind sooner rather than later.

articles.title: Jim Cramer says Costco's hefty special dividend signals ‘more gains ahead’
articles.text:
Costco is rewarding shareholders with a $30-per-share special dividend, and CNBC's Jim Cramer says history suggests that investors should stick around despite the catalyst moving into the rearview mirror.
The warehouse retailer announced its sixth special dividend last week, alongside a $4 billion share repurchase program. Shareholders of record as of Nov. 24 will receive the payout on Dec. 4. The company also pays a regular quarterly dividend of $1.47 that yields just 0.5% annually.
"With all due respect to the buyback program, which represents less than 1% of Costco's $490 billion market cap, it's the special dividend that I'm excited about," the "Mad Money" host said. "The sporadic special dividend is one of the unique privileges of owning Costco shares."
Costco issued its first special dividend in 2012 and has announced five more since then, with payouts arriving roughly every three years over the past decade. Together, those six payments have totaled $74 per share, on top of the company's regular quarterly dividend.
To be sure, given Costco's track record of these periodic extra payouts, some investors may view last week's announcement as a "buy the rumor, sell the news" situation. However, Cramer said in each of the past three instances — 2023, 2020 and 2017 — Costco shares have outperformed the S&P 500 over the next year.
"That's a very good verdict for those who wonder what to do with the stock now that the good news is out," Cramer said. "It says hold on, don't sell. More gains ahead."
There's also compelling math suggesting that investors should look to reinvest those dividends back into Costco's stock.
Cramer looked at investor returns over the past 15 years. A $1,000 investment in Costco's stock in November 2011 would have grown to approximately $13,321 through Friday, reflecting a 1,232% gain. But reinvesting all dividends into additional shares would have increased that investment's value to roughly $18,411, representing a 1,741% total return.
That's more than $5,000 in additional gains from reinvesting dividends rather than collecting the cash. Special dividends played an outsized role, accounting for roughly 64% of the $116 per share Costco paid in total dividends over that period. "That's an incredible case made for reinvesting of dividends," Cramer said.
"The sporadic special dividends have boosted this stock's total shareholder return meaningfully over the past decade-and-a-half, and they help keep you invested in the stock when it has its occasional lulls," he said.
Beyond boosting returns, the prospect of another special dividend gives investors an incentive to hold Costco through periods of weakness. That patience paid off this year, when shares retreated from nearly $1,100 in May into the high $800s before rebounding sharply this fall. The stock is now up 30% for the year.
"Sometimes I think that the stock's too expensive and it might be a good time to take profits," he said. "But then I remind myself that there's a good chance of a special dividend right around the corner, and it's so much easier to stick it out."

articles.title: Jim Cramer says Nvidia’s leadership shake-up won’t derail the AI trade
articles.text:
CNBC's Jim Cramer said Monday that Nvidia's leadership shake-up won't derail the artificial intelligence boom.
Cramer's comments came after another rough day for AI-related stocks in the wake of Jensen Huang's resignation from Nvidia last week. Investors have been worried that Huang's departure as CEO could jeopardize the chipmaker's financial support for the broader AI ecosystem, especially computing providers known as neoclouds. Nvidia is set to report earnings Tuesday night.
Cramer argued that demand for computing power extends far beyond Nvidia and its former CEO.
"The most important thing you need to know is that Nvidia is not going to bring down the western world," the "Mad Money" host said. "It is not going to bring down the data center world."
Under Huang, Nvidia built an extensive investment portfolio, including a $5 billion stake in Intel last year and an additional investment in AI cloud provider CoreWeave earlier this year. Nvidia had helped anchor CoreWeave's IPO in 2025 and participated in a 2023 Series B round for the company. In addition to taking equity stakes in other companies, Nvidia has provided other financial guarantees to customers, such as a $105 billion backstop for a sprawling data center project intended for OpenAI.
JPMorgan strategist Michael Cembalest, who publishes the closely followed Eye on the Market commentary, estimated that Nvidia's broader financial commitments may have reached $530 billion, based on the company's latest quarterly securities filing. Still, Cramer rejected the notion that the AI industry depends entirely on the chipmaker's backing.
"You can't overstate the importance of Jensen Huang to all of the AI investment that we've seen and expect to see," Cramer said. "But the idea that he was somehow all of the AI world is ludicrous."
Cramer expects interim CEO Colette Kress to take a more conservative approach, potentially scaling back some of Nvidia's financial commitments. While that could pressure heavily indebted companies, he said strong demand for computing power will sustain the broader AI build-out.
"Will there be a rein in of guarantees?" Cramer asked. "I hope so. Will Nvidia be more conservative? I am sure of it. Will artificial intelligence be stopped in its tracks? Are you kidding me?"
More generally, Cramer expressed confidence in Kress, praising her financial discipline and expecting a measured outlook when Nvidia reports earnings Tuesday. "I think interim CEO Kress will present a balanced non-hyperbolic view of the situations at Nvidia tomorrow night," he said. "I do not think it will cause a tsunami of selling."
A successful Anthropic IPO later this week could further restore confidence in the AI trade, Cramer argued.
"If the Anthropic deal works later this week, look out – we might see investors scrambling to get back into the same stocks that were sold today," Cramer said.

The Securities and Exchange Commission requires institutional investment managers, including hedge funds, to file quarterly holdings reports once they meet the $100 million in assets under management. Comparing these quarterly reports shows which stocks these managers are piling into and where they're pulling back. The filings reflect holdings as of Sept. 30, and managers may have changed their positions since then. Among notable buys during the period were D1 Capital Partners increasing its positions in Lattice Semiconductor and chip materials supplier Qnity Electronics . Coatue added to its stakes in two mega cap tech names, while Baupost pared its Alphabet holdings and opened a new position in Honeywell Aerospace . Check out CNBC's roundup of the biggest moves made by major investors in the third quarter. Appaloosa Appaloosa Management, led by legendary hedge fund manager David Tepper, opened new positions in Oracle , Applied Materials , Modine Manufacturing and PG & E during the third quarter. The firm's Oracle stake was worth $172 million by the end of the third quarter, while its Applied Materials position was valued at $115 million. The Modine Manufacturing holdings were worth $53 million, while the PG & E stake equated to $30.9 million in value. Appaloosa also closed positions in Apple put options, Advanced Micro Devices, Broadcom and Qualcomm. Apple and AMD both posted gains in the third quarter, while the latter two names pulled back. Baupost The Seth Klarman-led hedge fund initiated positions in industrial giant Honeywell Aerospace and SiteOne Landscape Supply . Those stakes were worth $175.4 million and $112.4 million, respectively, as of the end of the third quarter. During the third quarter, shares of Honeywell fell 30%, while SiteOne dropped 21% over the same period. The firm also trimmed its Alphabet stake by 31% and closed out its Norwegian Cruise position. Coatue Coatue, a hedge fund focused on technology investments, added significant amounts of capital to two megacap tech names while initiating a position in a beaten-down software stock. The fund boosted its Microsoft holdings by 120% quarter over quarter, with its position worth $3.31 billion by the end of the period, up from $1.1 billion in the second quarter. It also increased its Meta position by 79%, with the stake valued at $3.27 billion. While shares of the social media giant gained more than 28% during the third quarter, Meta has gotten punished since reporting negative free cash flow for the period in late October. The stock has fallen more than 11% over the past month over investor concerns that the company continues to spend too aggressively on AI-related infrastructure. Microsoft stock is faring much better. During Q3, the software giant gained 38%. The market favored the company's cloud growth during its latest third quarter earnings. Coatue also started a position in Salesforce worth $1.84 billion. The stock has tumbled 17% year to date over concerns that artificial intelligence tools could make its customer management platform obsolete. D1 Capital D1 Capital Partners increased its Lattice Semiconductor by 462%, with the stake worth to $765 million at the end of the third quarter. Lattice, which designs and manufactures control chips for servers and data centers, fell 3.7% on Monday, getting hit along with its semiconductor peers. The stock still has a strong showing for 2026, gaining 47% year to date. The firm sharply increased its Qnity Electronics position, with the stake now worth $642 million in Q3 from $136 million in the second quarter. Qnity, which was spun off from DuPont, is a key supplier of chemicals and materials used in semiconductor and electronics manufacturing. On top of that, D1 Capital initiated a position in Viking Holdings valued at $314 million. The global cruise liner is scheduled to report earnings Tuesday before the bell. The stock is up 25% year-to-date. Another big bet made by D1 was upping its Amazon stake by nearly 60%, with the position worth $250 million at the end of the third quarter. Tiger Global Management Tiger Global made a series of stock purchases across the tech sector along with several new additions to the portfolio. One of its larger purchases was in Danaher, with the Chase Coleman-led fund boosting its position in the stock by 178%. The stake was worth $281 million at the end of Q3. The company is known for making instruments, tools and technologies for biotechnology and diagnostics. The stock has been on an uptrend throughout the back half of 2026 and has gained 42% over the past six months. Tiger Global also upped its stake in Cerebras Systems by 48% to $789 million. Cerebras builds giant chips and supercomputers designed to process large AI workloads quickly. The firm made a few new additions to its portfolio, including Ferrari, Bending Spoons and Xanadu Quantum Technologies. It also cut its Alphabet stake by 42% and sold 46% of its Apollo Global shares.

articles.title: Stock futures are little changed after Nvidia pressures tech to start the week: Live updates
articles.text:
Stock futures were little changed on Monday night, following a losing session as Nvidia once again dragged down the tech sector.
Dow Jones Industrial Average futures inched up 8 points, or 0.02%. S&P 500 futures were up 0.06%, while Nasdaq-100 futures advanced 0.1%
Asia-Pacific markets opened lower Tuesday. Japan's Nikkei 225 fell 0.76%, while the Topix declined 1.06%. South Korea's Kospi dropped 1.57%, while the small-cap Kosdaq lost 0.62%. Australia's S&P/ASX 200 declined 1.37%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index fell 1.17%, while mainland China's CSI 300 opened flat.
In regular U.S. trading, Nvidia shares pulled back 4.1%, as traders dumped the chipmaker ahead of its fiscal third-quarter report, due Tuesday after the bell. Other stocks linked to the artificial intelligence trade fell as well, including AMD, Micron Technology and Sandisk.
"The tape feels increasingly fragile as Nvidia's AI premium continues to unwind and investors reassess the durability of the ecosystem built around its dominance," said Ben Emons, founder of FedWatch Advisors, in a note. "This backdrop has fueled the 'dispersion trade,' gradually eroding the extreme concentration that has defined the S&P 500 and Nasdaq."
Nvidia has been tumbling since last week. Jensen Huang resigned from the CEO post Thursday after reports emerged that he had multiple affairs, including one with an alleged Chinese spy. Further, the chipmaker's board of directors is not considering bringing Huang back as CEO, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The stock has dropped almost 24% this month, putting it on pace for its biggest monthly decline since April 2022 — when it plunged 32%.
The 30-stock Dow on Monday slid more than 700 points, or 1.4%, while the S&P 500 lost 1.9%. The tech-heavy Nasdaq Composite dropped 2.5%, its biggest one-day decline since Nov. 5.
On Tuesday, investors will pore through a slew of economic data, including October retail sales and import prices. On the earnings front, Disney and Home Depot are set to report before the opening bell.

articles.title: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: As Nike and Lululemon struggle in China, Xiaohongshu is helping local brands take off
articles.text:
Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses.
While the world watched the Nvidia saga around Jensen Huang unfold, Chinese retailers quietly wrapped up the local version of Black Friday, known as Singles Day. What can foreign brands learn?
The big story
As Lululemon, On Running and other Western consumer brands have sought to expand in China, so have a crop of local brands with English names.
Monday Sleeping Club, Crying Center, AW Project, an action a day, Liegee. The list of trendy new Chinese brands has grown rapidly, despite flatlining retail sales nationwide.
"Their success rests on one shared formula," said Cynthia Zhang, analyst, Euromonitor International.
"Build a non-product asset first — credible fabric quality, an emotion, an aesthetic reputation, or proprietary fit data — then monetize it through founder-led content, Xiaohongshu-driven discovery, tight supply chains, and the quiet-luxury and Guochao [national pride] mood that prizes craftsmanship over conspicuous logos," she said.
For Liegee, one of its three founders, Cocoa Lin, told me its sales surged by roughly 160% during the latest Singles Day period to the tens of millions of yuan, equivalent to a few million U.S. dollars.
The brand launched in 2022 in Hangzhou to meet a perceived gap in clothes for early career women looking to express their personality, Lin said. She said the brand, which has over 100,000 fans for its store on Alibaba's Taobao e-commerce site, largely uses internet influencers and celebrity product seeding to generate awareness.
The brand uses Xiaohongshu, on which it has over 22,000 followers, for catalog-style photos and marketing videos. It opened a "Liegee Motel" pop-up in Shenzhen last month.
"We believe online and offline will have a closer connection in the future," Lin said in Mandarin via translation, adding that "as lifestyles become more experience-oriented, this energy can be transmitted to online."
It's a dynamic that Western brands have struggled to crack.
Nike reported a 22% sales drop in Greater China in the quarter ended Aug. 31, while Lululemon reported a 2% drop in mainland China comparable sales in the quarter ended Aug. 2.
But Adidas recorded a 20% increase.
Adidas runs at least six official Xiaohongshu accounts, with two notching well over 200,000 followers each. Nike and Lululemon each operate one official account, with over 300,000 followers each.
For a country of around 1.4 billion people, Xiaohongshu has captured a key consumer audience.
The social media app, whose layout is a mix of Instagram and Pinterest, has focused on women and young people in China's largest cities, and recent expanded into less developed parts of the country, according to Questmobile. Xiaohongshu recorded average daily users of 120 million in October, a fraction of the 422 million on Taobao and 717 million on Douyin, the report showed.
The app has also attempted to build up its own e-commerce business in order to monetize.
"RedNote [or Xiaohongshu] has been a key platform for product discovery and research, especially for female consumers shopping in the beauty, skincare, lifestyle, fashion, and health categories. Now, we're seeing more transactions within RedNote itself," said Jacob Cooke, co-founder and CEO of WPIC Marketing + Technologies. The company helps foreign brands sell in China and other parts of Asia.
Alibaba, JD.com and ByteDance's Douyin still dominated this year's Singles Day sales with a combined 1.68 trillion yuan in sales over the Oct. 7 to Nov. 11 period, according to Syntun.
What's changed more fundamentally is the mood of the Chinese consumer, including more affluent ones.
In the era of double-digit annual growth in real estate prices, consumers pursued conspicuous consumption to meet "aspirational" desires, Christine Peng, head of Greater China consumer research, UBS, told reporters last week.
"Now those needs no longer exist," she said in Mandarin, translated by CNBC.
"The rise of these trendy brands reflects how consumers now seek to define their own identities and pursue personal enjoyment, while still remaining mindful of price and quality," Peng said.
She said wealthy consumers are also embracing domestic brands, and no longer just buying traditional luxury brands.
Need to know
Alice Huang tied to Nvidia's biggest Chinese competitor
Alice Huang has owned stakes in companies that have benefited Huawei, private intelligence firm Tesari shared exclusively with CNBC. Some in Beijing worry the Jensen Huang affair will negatively impact U.S.-China relations.
China's goods surplus tops $1 trillion
Exports in October jumped by 35.2%, while imports soared 41.6%, both beating Reuters' estimates. But industrial output, retail sales and investment figures for October all missed estimates. China and the U.S. discussed tariffs and agricultural trade ahead of Xi-Trump meeting, the Chinese Commerce Ministry said Saturday.
Alibaba announces plans to list T-Head, its Nvidia chip rival
The Chinese tech company disclosed the Hong Kong Stock Exchange will allow it to spin off its semiconductor subsidiary T-Head.
Coming up
Nov. 17: Nvidia earnings
Nov. 18 - 19: APEC Economic Leaders' Meeting in Shenzhen
Nov. 18: Tencent earnings

articles.title: Aschenbrenner’s Situational Awareness made AI bets again before October rout
articles.text:
Leopold Aschenbrenner's artificial intelligence-themed hedge fund Situational Awareness, which nearly collapsed in July, loaded back up on AI stocks as it returned to the financial markets at the end of the third quarter. But all of its holdings are down big the last month and a half.
According to a new regulatory filing, as the fund got back on its feet Aschenbrenner took an equity position in Australian neocloud company SharonAI valued at more than $440 million, along with equity stakes in AI-centric plays Cleanspark, IREN, Bitdeer Technologies and Fermi. The Cleanspark stake is worth almost $39 million, while Iren and Bitdeer stakes are more than $21 million and more than $20 million, respectively. Fermi, meanwhile, has a value of more than $11 million.
The fund also owned call options at the end of September in neocloud Nebius, memory chip name Sandisk, the Roundhill Memory ETF (DRAM) and data center power play Bloom Energy. Sandisk and Nebius were key holdings that almost took out his fund over the summer.
All of these Situational Awareness holdings have been routed since Sept. 30. SharonAI is at the top of that list, seeing a 58% loss in October. It's also fallen 11% so far this month. IREN was down 41% in October, while Nebius declined 35%. Last week, Nebius plummeted more than 16% in a single day after the company issued a weak full-year forecast.
It's not known whether the hedge fund manager got out of those positions during the October AI selloff. The 13F filing is just a snapshot of what the hedge fund held at the end of the quarter.
Aschenbrenner — who launched the fund in 2024 after rising to fame that same year with his AI manifesto also entitled Situational Awareness — re-entered financial markets a bit in September, sources told CNBC at the time.
The Monday filing shows he picked up right where he left off.
The near-collapse of his hedge fund over the summer forced him to sell all of its public equity positions to Ken Griffin's Citadel. The fund had $45 billion in assets at its peak, but that tumbled to around $10 billion, consisting mostly of private stakes.
Stocked tethered to the AI trade took a hit in the most recent quarter as investors grew concerned about a slowdown in development of the technology. Those fears were spurred by comments from industry leaders such as Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei and OpenAI CEO Sam Altman back in September, with the latter saying that the company going public this year would be "ill-advised."
Since then, pressure on the trade has only continued.
In recent weeks, investors have worried about how Democratic wins in the midterm elections could hinder data center development, whether some technology companies are using too much debt to finance the AI buildout and what role Nvidia will play in that financing with Jensen Huang now out as CEO at the company.
Losses in Nvidia as well as other AI-related stocks dragged down the three leading U.S. indexes during Monday's session as investors continued to assess the fallout of Huang's departure.

articles.title: Berkshire Hathaway raised its stake in Delta in the third quarter. It also trimmed a key bank holding
articles.text:
Berkshire Hathaway made several moves in the stock market during the third quarter, adding to key positions and trimming others.
The Omaha-based conglomerate, now led by CEO Greg Abel, increased its Delta Air Lines stake by 12%, scooping up 7.13 million shares. The position was worth $5.37 billion at the end of the third quarter.
Abel succeeded legendary investor Warren Buffett, 96, at the start of this year. Buffett continues to control roughly 13% of Berkshire common stock, Reuters said Monday, after the former CEO donated $5.5 billion to nonprofit foundations.
Berkshire boosted its stake in Delta as the Atlanta-based carrier's shares tumbled 11% in the third quarter, hurt by rising jet fuel prices due to the U.S.-Iran war that pressured the entire airline industry. That marked the stock's worst quarterly performance since the first quarter of 2025, when it plunged 28%. Delta last month also cut its full-year earnings forecast, citing a surge in fuel costs.
To be sure, buying that dip has been a winning investment thus far. Delta is up 3.8% so far in the fourth quarter, while the S&P 500 has dropped 3.1%. Shares are also up nearly 15% over the past month.
Selling some Bank of America
Berkshire also trimmed its holding in Bank of America by nearly 6%, selling more than $1.6 billion worth of stock.
BofA was under pressure in the third quarter, falling more than 4%, as interest rates surged alongside stubbornly high inflation and expectations of tighter Federal Reserve monetary policy. At one point in September the 30-year Treasury bond yield surged above 5.6% to its highest level since 2002.
Despite the share sale, Bank of America remains a top Berkshire Hathaway holding, with the conglomerate's stake valued at $24.8 billion at the end of the third quarter.
Berkshire also initiated a position in Bending Spoons and nearly doubled its stake in homebuilder Lennar in the latest quarter.

articles.title: United Airlines resolves system outage that affected departing flights
articles.text:
United Airlines on Monday said it had resolved a "widespread system outage" that briefly affected departing flights.
"We have resolved a technology issue that delayed flight departures," the airline said in a statement. "While some flights were delayed, there was no impact on flights in progress, or on United Express flights.
A United spokesperson said there was no indication that the outage was a cyberattack.
The Air Line Pilots Association, which represents pilots for United and other carriers, said in an earlier message to members seen by CNBC that the operational outage was "affecting multiple pilot facing applications" and that United could not "provide outbound flights with final weights."
United's outage came three days after a nationwide ground stop halted departures across the country for more than four hours, snarling travel and leading to widespread delays and cancellations over the weekend.
Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy blamed the issues that led to Friday's ground stop on a router in Arkansas that overwhelmed systems that feed radar and other data for air traffic control. Federal Aviation Administration Administrator Bryan Bedford said the upgrades were part of "routine" maintenance to switch over from copper wires to fiber optic.
There were significantly fewer flight delays and cancellations Monday than had been reported Sunday, according to FlightAware data.
There was no indication that United's outage Monday was related to the issues that caused Friday's ground stop.
— CNBC's Leslie Josephs and Phil LeBeau contributed to this report.

articles.title: Trump’s accounts traded up to $97.5 million in Nvidia as Huang gained White House access
articles.text:
President Donald Trump has had plenty of reason to cheer the rise of Nvidia.
The chipmaker helped propel the stock market that Trump is fond of touting. Its billionaire co-founder, Jensen Huang, became one of the president's favorite businessmen. And by the end of last year, Nvidia had become one of Trump's three largest individual stock holdings, worth between $12.5 million and $58 million, up from between $615,000 and $1.3 million a year earlier.
Since returning to the White House, Trump's investment accounts have bought or sold Nvidia shares at least 103 times — transactions worth a combined $27 million to $97.5 million, according to a new CNBC analysis of his annual and periodic financial disclosures, which were most recently updated through August.
By midday Monday, Trump's Nvidia stake, based on the value he reported holding in August, would be worth $4.5 million to $57.7 million with stock priced around $157. But the filings give broad dollar ranges for holdings rather than the number of shares, leaving his current stake unclear.
Now, Huang's resignation as Nvidia's CEO on Thursday, following revelations about his relationship with a woman suspected of spying for China and reports of affairs with company employees, has put those trades back in the spotlight.
Among them was a sale of $500,001 to $1 million on May 18, the first Monday after Trump returned from a state visit to China with Huang. Five days earlier, before Huang boarded Air Force One during a refueling stop in Alaska, Secretary of State Marco Rubio had briefed Trump on intelligence concerning Huang's relationship with the suspected spy, The New York Times reported.
Trump on Monday denied being briefed. Asked about the reported briefing from Rubio, Trump said, "I haven't heard that," adding that he did not know whether the woman, Alice Huang, was a Chinese spy.
The president's financial accounts also bought smaller amounts of Nvidia shares in the days immediately before and after the May 18 sale, part of a broader trading blitz. Such flurries have defined his second term: Trump disclosed more than 21,000 trades in 2025 alone, compared with roughly 500 during his entire first term, according to CNBC's analysis.
A White House spokesperson told CNBC independent advisors manage Trump's portfolio without his input. Trump Organization spokesperson Kimberly Benza said the arrangement is designed to "avoid even the appearance of a conflict of interest." The disclosures offer no evidence Trump directed the trades or that his advisors had access to classified intelligence.
Trump has long used the stock market as a scorecard for the economy, touting its record highs — sometimes when highs have not actually been reached — despite the turbulence caused by his tariffs and the Iran war.
"Look, we have the highest stock market we've ever had," Trump told ESPN commentator and political talk show host Stephen A. Smith on Thursday when pressed about Republicans' midterm losses.
Nvidia alone accounted for about 13.5% of the S&P 500's 2026 gains through September, according to an analysis by Choate Wealth that looked at how chip stocks have driven the year's performance.
Huang's rise in Trump's Washington has been nearly as striking as Nvidia's on Wall Street. The two have met or appeared together at least 15 times since Trump returned to office, according to a CNBC review of public records and news reports. Huang in June told The Associated Press that Trump even "calls me in the middle of the night."
It wasn't always that way.
At Trump's Jan. 20, 2025, inauguration, several Silicon Valley titans occupied prime seats, but Huang wasn't there. The two men had never met.
That changed on Jan. 31, 2025, when Huang visited the White House, capping a bruising week for Nvidia: Chinese AI startup DeepSeek had wiped $593 billion off the company's market value in a single day, according to LSEG data cited by Reuters.
Two days before the meeting, Trump's money managers bought between $1 million and $5 million in Nvidia stock.
For Huang, much of the relationship hinged on access to China. In April 2025, the administration effectively halted sales of Nvidia's H20 chips to China, prompting a $4.5 billion charge, according to an SEC filing. Huang argued that withholding U.S. chips would only accelerate China's development of its own.
The administration eventually relented. After another meeting with Trump in July 2025, Huang announced from Beijing that Nvidia expected to resume H20 sales. A week after Trump confirmed an August 2025 deal calling for 15% of the revenue from the company's chip sales to China to go to the U.S. government, his accounts also bought between $5 million and $25 million in Nvidia stock, one of several large tech investments that day.
Huang was also becoming a fixture of Trump's international diplomacy, joining him in Saudi Arabia and the U.K. Nvidia, already a $1 million donor to Trump's inaugural fund, would pledge another $25 million to his planned White House ballroom on condition of anonymity, The Washington Post first reported.
But behind the scenes, intelligence officials first briefed Trump last fall on Huang's relationship with the woman suspected of spying for China, The New York Times reported.
Trump nevertheless continued to ease restrictions on Nvidia's business in China, announcing Dec. 8 that the company could sell its more powerful H200 chips. His accounts had sold as much as $1 million in Nvidia stock four days earlier and bought more the day after.
In the first eight months of 2026, Trump's accounts made another 38 Nvidia trades worth a combined $9.4 million to $28.3 million, according to CNBC's analysis. A disclosure released Oct. 8 — the day Trump awarded Huang the National Medal of Science — showed purchases of up to $1.6 million and sales of up to $1 million in August alone.
Trump stood by Huang as Nvidia's board weighed his future last week, urging him to fight to keep his job, the Times reported.
With Huang out and Nvidia's shares tumbling, Trump described him Thursday as a "tremendous talent" who was "going through hell" — in the same interview in which he boasted of the market's record highs.
Trump is already floating a comeback for Huang, telling reporters Monday that reinstating him "certainly isn't a bad idea." But Nvidia's board is not considering his return, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC. The person asked not to be named because they were discussing internal matters."

articles.title: JPMorgan Chase says temporary software bug is affecting consumer banking
articles.text:
JPMorgan Chase reported a "technical issue" that was affecting some consumer banking services Monday.
The bank said a "temporary issue related to a software bug in on-premise hardware systems" was causing some customer transactions to take longer than usual, though it said customers can still access their accounts and funds.
"There is no evidence it is cyber-related," a JPMorgan spokesperson said in a statement to CNBC.
"This is not a systemic issue — other banks may have been impacted by slowness in transactions only to the extent that they were a party to a transaction with us," the spokesperson said. "We're working diligently to resolve this by the end of the day today."
CNBC's Eamon Javers reported there was no indication of bad actors involved.
Still, other major banks were listed in outage reports as transactions between Chase and other institutions appeared to get held up. Users reported errors as early as 11:30 a.m. ET.
A representative for U.S. Bank said that company was "not directly impacted. However, clients attempting to send or receive Zelle payments with another financial institution may experience transaction delays."
Zelle is the peer-to-peer payments system backed by many of the largest U.S. banks, including JPMorgan.
The outage reports come days after separate, widespread issues with Microsoft Outlook and communication systems used by air traffic control centers.
— CNBC's Leslie Picker contributed to this report.

articles.title: Kalshi plans to launch stock trading soon
articles.text:
Leading prediction market platform Kalshi will offer stock trading within the next few months, a person familiar with the matter told CNBC.
The platform's move to offer equity trading is the boldest so far in its ongoing push into traditional financial markets and comes amid an escalating fight by states and lawmakers against its sports trading business. Sports contracts continue to account for a large share of trading on the platform.
In September, the platform introduced perpetual futures tied to precious metals such as gold and silver after it had originally filed in July to offer beyond prediction market event contracts with the Commodity Futures Trading Commission, the federal regulator overseeing derivatives contracts. Perpetual futures are futures-style contracts that have no expiration date.
Kalshi also received approval to list perpetual futures tied to cryptocurrencies in late May.
The prediction market's stock trading offering was enabled by its purchase of broker-dealer FB Securities in July, the source said. FB Securities was founded in Delaware in 2024 and became registered with the Securities and Exchange Commission in December 2025. The broker did not respond to a request for comment.
The Wall Street Journal first reported that Kalshi plans to introduce stock trading.
Shares of Robinhood, which offers some prediction markets alongside equity trading, fell on Monday, though the stock was already lower amid a broader market sell-off. Robinhood closed down by 7.8%.
Disclosure: CNBC and Kalshi have a commercial relationship that includes customer acquisition and a minority investment.

articles.title: Eli Lilly makes a deal outside obesity. Plus, another word of caution on Nvidia
articles.text: Every weekday, the CNBC Investing Club with Jim Cramer releases the Homestretch — an actionable afternoon update, just in time for the last hour of trading on Wall Street. The market remains volatile as questions about the durability of the AI infrastructure theme weigh on Wall Street. The S & P 500 fell by about 1.8%, and the tech-heavy Nasdaq dropped even more. The AI trade came under pressure from uncertainty surrounding Nvidia's future role as a financial backstop for the broader AI buildout, as well as the Commerce Department's move to close a loophole that allowed Chinese companies to rent Nvidia's computing power in other countries remotely. Only one sector on Monday was solidly positive: consumer staples, which is home to Club stocks like Costco , Kimberly-Clark , and Constellation Brands . Investors have been gravitating toward the staples group for its slower but dependable growth and consistent dividend and share repurchase programs. We've made similar moves over the past few months, selling out of tech names like Corning and Broadcom, and adding Kimberly-Clark and Constellation to the portfolio to further diversify the portfolio away from the AI trade. The staples sector is up 20% this year, making it the third best-performing sector this year behind energy and healthcare. Information technology's 3% drop on Monday pushed the sector's gains this year below 10%. Let's spend a little more time on Nvidia, as we approach earnings Tuesday night. At the moment, we are considering the stock more of a "not rated" than the hold-equivalent 2 we downgraded it to last Tuesday. The reason why is that there is so much uncertainty at the company following Jensen Huang resignation as CEO. The larger questions we simply do not know the answer to relate to the company continuing to provide financial support to other companies in the AI ecosystem; whether management will stand by its 70% revenue growth forecast for fiscal year 2028; and the earnings risks associated with a potential tightening of U.S. export controls to Southeast Asia (beyond the aforementioned Commerce Department decision). These unknowns are why Jim recommended taking some shares off the table on Thursday as a matter of capital preservation, and he reiterated that view earlier Monday. Johnson & Johnson wasn't the only pharma company in our portfolio that struck a deal Monday. Eli Lilly has agreed to acquire to acquire Calytrix Bio for up to $1.5 billion, Calytrix announced in a press release. The privately held biotech is working on an early-stage antibody treatment for rare blood disorders. It's a small deal that doesn't move the needle any time soon, but the acquisition is fitting of Lilly's broader M & A strategy of using its GLP-1 windfall to expand its portfolio beyond its core obesity franchise. Lilly has stepped up the pace of dealmaking this year. In a BiotechTV interview published Oct. 7, CEO David Ricks said Lilly had already done 40 deals year to date, more than all of 2025. Last year Lilly averaged one transaction "every two weeks," Ricks told the outlet. "Now we're doing like one a week." Separately, analysts at Barclays raised their Lilly price target to $1,550 from $1,400 on Monday. The bump was mostly tied to the analysts updating their models after Lilly's blockbuster third-quarter earnings report . Barclays pointed to Lilly's upcoming innovation day on Dec. 7 as an opportunity where management can outline its growth opportunities beyond obesity. Aecom reports after the closing bell on Monday. Home Depot , Disney , Viking Holdings , Klarna , Amer Sports , and JD.com report before the opening bell on Tuesday. On the data side, we'll see the October retail sales report. articles.title: Jim Cramer says J&J is a 'metaphor for what's working' in the stock market
articles.text: Johnson & Johnson is a prime example of the kind of stock doing well in the broader market as investors shy away from the volatile artificial intelligence trade. "[J & J] is a metaphor for what's working," Jim Cramer said Monday on CNBC, as shares of the pharma and medtech giant hit another all-time high before reversing lower in a terrible market. Investors have been rotating into defensive sectors, such as healthcare and consumer staples, as stocks tied to the AI boom have fallen on hard times. It's an evolving dynamic Jim has been capitalizing on in recent weeks as the Club has been trimming data center exposure and diversifying into defensives. It was a big part of our Annual Meeting earlier this month. Over the past month, healthcare and consumer staples are the market's two top performers, with gains of 7% and 6%, respectively, crushing the S & P 500 's nearly 3% decline. Tech, over the same stretch, is down more than 9%, due to concerns about what the Democratic wave in the midterm elections might mean for the data center buildout. The fallout from the leadership scandal at Nvidia has added to the uncertainty. "J & J is the exact opposite of Nvidia. It's a clean company. Everybody loves J & J," Jim added. We initiated a position in Johnson & Johnson in early April. The stock is up 20% since then, logging a record-high close Friday. Shares opened higher Monday after the company announced it's buying clinical-stage biopharmaceutical company Ollin Biosciences for $2.2 billion up front and another up to $1.13 billion if certain milestones are met. This deal will expand J & J's treatments for serious eye diseases. JNJ YTD mountain Johnson & Johnson YTD Jim has been bullish on J & J for quite some time, noting the company's strong pipeline of drugs. This includes its leading blood cancer treatments and newer products, like Icotyde , its one-of-a-kind oral solution for plaque psoriasis. Plus, J & J managed to mitigate a major legal headwind stemming from its talc products that weighed on the company for years. Beyond that, Jim pointed to J & J's strong fundamentals and management's ability to execute well. Last month, J & J delivered better-than-expected revenue and earnings for the third quarter. The stock, however, dropped nearly 6%, due to disappointing performance in the MedTech segment and the tendency for shares to trade poorly on earnings day. Jim argued that investors sometimes overlook the company's underlying results immediately following quarterly releases, only to recognize its strength later. As we wrote in our Q3 earnings analysis , "A big reason why we're comfortable looking past the weakness in MedTech is that there's so much to like on the pharmaceutical side." The company is taking steps to boost MedTech growth potential, with a planned spin-off of its orthopedics business by 2027. Next month, J & J is set to report its fourth-quarter results. articles.title: Ăn thử bánh dày giò cả Hà Nội đang nô nức tìm ăn: Chỉ 15k/cặp, khách ngồi điều hoà uống trà nhài miễn phí
articles.text:
Ăn thử bánh dày giò cả Hà Nội đang nô nức tìm ăn: Chỉ 15k/cặp, khách ngồi điều hoà uống trà nhài miễn phí
Từ món quà sáng quen thuộc của người Hà Nội, bánh dày giò bất ngờ trở thành món ăn được nhiều bạn trẻ săn lùng. Cùng một chiếc bánh dẻo mềm kẹp giò lụa hay chả mỡ, nhưng khi thử tại 3 địa chỉ nổi tiếng, mỗi nơi lại có một điểm cộng riêng.
- 17-11-2026Miền Bắc sắp đón không khí lạnh liên tiếp
- 17-11-2026Vì sao Hà Nội cấm trồng loài cây quen thuộc với người Việt, quả làm thức ăn cho chim, nhựa dùng phủ đồ nội thất?
- 17-11-2026Dự báo thời tiết ngày 17/11: Miền Bắc nắng trên 32°C trước khi chuyển mưa rét
Không phải món ăn cầu kỳ hay có cách chế biến mới lạ, bánh dày giò vốn là thức quà sáng quen thuộc của nhiều thế hệ người Hà Nội. Một cặp bánh trắng muốt, dẻo mềm, kẹp bên trong miếng giò lụa hoặc chả mỡ, vừa đủ gọn nhẹ cho bữa sáng, vừa có mức giá bình dân. Thế nhưng thời gian gần đây, món ăn tưởng chừng chẳng có gì mới mẻ này lại bất ngờ trở thành cái tên được nhiều bạn trẻ tìm kiếm.
Một trong những lý do khiến bánh dày giò được chú ý là những video review trên mạng xã hội. Đáng kể, nhà sáng tạo nội dung Minh Tỷ từng khiến người xem thích thú khi vừa thưởng thức bánh dày vừa tự nhận mình là “công chúa giò chả”, “con dâu vua Hùng”. Cách nói chuyện hài hước, dí dỏm cùng hình ảnh những miếng giò, miếng chả to được kẹp trong chiếc bánh dày dẻo mềm khiến không ít người tò mò muốn thử.
Từ những video review, nhiều hàng giò chả lâu năm lẫn những địa chỉ được giới thiệu trên mạng xã hội bắt đầu lọt vào danh sách phải thử của các tín đồ ẩm thực. Và khi một món ăn có giá chỉ vài chục nghìn đồng cũng đủ khiến người ta rủ nhau đi trải nghiệm, câu hỏi đặt ra là: Bánh dày giò ở những địa chỉ nổi tiếng có thực sự khác biệt, và đâu mới là nơi đáng để ghé thử?
Team Có Như Lời Đồn đã tìm đến 3 địa chỉ gồm Giò chả Thuỷ Hùng ở ngõ 252 Tây Sơn, Giò chả Nam Anh tại 41 Đường Thành và bánh dày giò cô Hải ở số 8 Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm để trực tiếp trải nghiệm.
1. Giò chả Thuỷ Hùng: 15.000 đồng/cặp, có chỗ ngồi sạch sẽ, trà nhài đá miễn phí
Nếu thường xuyên theo dõi các video review đồ ăn trên mạng xã hội, có lẽ bạn đã bắt gặp hình ảnh những chiếc bánh dày kẹp giò, kẹp chả tại Giò chả Ước Lễ nghệ nhân Thuỷ Hùng. Nằm trong ngõ 252 Tây Sơn, Hà Đông, địa chỉ này thu hút sự chú ý của nhiều bạn trẻ sau những video được chia sẻ rộng rãi.
Ấn tượng đầu tiên của chúng tôi khi đến đây là không gian khá khác biệt so với hình dung về một hàng giò chả truyền thống. Quán sạch sẽ, rộng rãi, có quạt và điều hoà, bật nhạc trẻ, bố trí khoảng 5-6 bộ bàn ghế cả trong lẫn ngoài. Thay vì chỉ mua đồ rồi mang đi, khách hoàn toàn có thể ngồi lại thưởng thức ngay tại chỗ. Cảm giác lúc này giống ghé một quán ăn nhỏ hơn là một cửa hàng giò chả chuyên bán mang đi.
Khu chế biến nằm bên trong nhà cũng gọn gàng, sạch sẽ. Giò chả được đựng trong các khay inox, nhân viên thao tác nhanh nhẹn, nhiệt tình. Khi khách gọi món, giò chả được thái và cân trước khi thanh toán. Chỉ ít phút sau, bánh dày đã được chuẩn bị sẵn trên đĩa để khách mang ra bàn.
Điều khiến team bất ngờ hơn cả là giá bán. Một cặp bánh dày kẹp giò hoặc chả tại đây có giá chỉ 15.000 đồng. Chúng tôi gọi hai cặp, một bánh dày giò lụa và một bánh dày chả mỡ, tổng cộng hết 30.000 đồng.
Với bánh dày kẹp giò lụa, miếng giò có kích thước khá lớn, độ dày vừa phải, ăn vừa miệng. Giò có vị tươi, thơm, không bị bở. Phần bánh dày bên ngoài trắng muốt, mềm mịn, dẻo dính nhưng không cứng hay dai quá mức. Khi ăn cùng nhau, bánh và giò tạo thành một món quà sáng đơn giản nhưng dễ ăn, không cần thêm thắt quá nhiều gia vị.
Nếu giò lụa mang đến cảm giác quen thuộc thì bánh dày kẹp chả mỡ lại là món khiến chúng tôi thích thú hơn. Miếng chả khá to, khi ăn vẫn còn ấm nóng. Cắn một miếng, phần chả mềm, béo và mọng nước, tạo cảm giác đầy đặn trong miệng. So với mức giá 15.000 đồng/cặp, phần nhân như vậy là khá hào phóng.
Một chi tiết nhỏ nhưng cũng đáng để cộng điểm là nhân viên không kéo giãn bánh dày để bọc kín phần nhân như cách một số hàng thường làm. Bánh được giữ nguyên hình dáng, kẹp giò hoặc chả ở giữa. Cách trình bày này có thể không quá cầu kỳ, nhưng phần bánh và nhân vẫn cân đối, dễ ăn.
Ngoài chất lượng món ăn, trải nghiệm tại Thuỷ Hùng còn được cộng điểm nhờ một chi tiết tưởng nhỏ mà hữu ích: trà nhài đá miễn phí, khách có thể tự phục vụ. Sau khi ăn bánh dày kẹp chả mỡ, có sẵn một cốc trà mát để uống cùng khiến bữa ăn dễ chịu hơn hẳn.
Không chỉ bán bánh dày giò, chả, cửa hàng còn có nhiều loại giò chả và đồ ăn bình dân khác. Chả mỡ có giá 16.000 đồng/lạng, chả cốm và chả quế 18.000 đồng/lạng. Giò lụa, giò xào, giò tai, giò bò, giò gà cũng được bán riêng theo trọng lượng. Bánh dày không có giá 5.000 đồng/cặp; bánh giò 15.000 đồng; bánh mì giò lụa hoặc chả nướng 20.000 đồng; bánh mì giò chả, chả cốm 25.000 đồng và bánh mì thập cẩm 30.000 đồng.
Với những ai muốn mua thêm đồ ăn vặt hoặc mang về, quán còn bán nem chua, nem chua rán, nem chua phô mai, nem bùi, giò xào, lạc rang, muối vừng và cả sữa đậu, tào phớ.
Điểm chúng mình chấm: 10/10. Không gian sạch sẽ, có điều hoà, phục vụ nhanh, bánh dày và nhân đều ngon trong khi mức giá lại mềm nhất trong ba địa chỉ đã thử. Nếu muốn tìm một nơi vừa ăn bánh dày giò, vừa có thể ngồi nghỉ ngơi thoải mái, Thuỷ Hùng là cái tên khiến chúng tôi hài lòng nhất.
2. Giò chả Nam Anh: Bánh thơm mùi nước mắm, nhân đậm đà, ăn hai chiếc đã thấy no
Nằm tại số 41 Đường Thành, Giò chả Nam Anh cũng là một địa chỉ được nhiều người biết đến khi nhắc tới giò chả tại Hà Nội. Cửa hàng nhận được nhiều đánh giá tích cực trên Google Maps, với mức điểm 4,8/5 theo thông tin chúng tôi ghi nhận.
Khác với Thuỷ Hùng, Nam Anh mang dáng dấp của một cửa hàng giò chả truyền thống chuyên bán mang đi. Quầy chế biến được bố trí ngay trước mặt tiền, khách có thể quan sát các loại giò, chả, ruốc, bánh mì, bánh chưng và lạc rang được bày trong tủ kính.
Không gian ở đây không có khu vực ngồi ăn rộng rãi như Thuỷ Hùng. Khách chủ yếu ghé mua đồ rồi mang đi, phù hợp với những người đang cần một bữa sáng nhanh gọn hoặc muốn mua thêm giò chả mang về nhà.
Bù lại, Nam Anh có danh mục sản phẩm khá đa dạng. Ngoài các loại giò lụa, giò bò, giò bê, giò gà, giò tai nấm, giò xào và chả quế, cửa hàng còn bán chả cốm, chả lợn, chả bò, chả cua, chả mực, chả tôm, chả cá, chân giò muối cùng một số loại thịt khô, dăm bông.
Về giá cả, bánh dày giò tại đây có nhiều mức giá, từ 20.000 đến 30.000 đồng/cặp tuỳ loại. Chúng tôi chọn hai cặp bánh dày, một kẹp giò lụa và một kẹp chả mỡ, với mức giá 20.000 đồng/cặp, tổng cộng 40.000 đồng.
Điểm khác biệt dễ nhận ra khi thưởng thức bánh dày Nam Anh nằm ở mùi thơm và độ đậm đà của phần nhân. Cả bánh dày kẹp giò lụa lẫn bánh dày kẹp chả đều có hương thơm rõ hơn, đặc biệt là mùi nước mắm đặc trưng. Khi ăn, vị giò chả cũng đậm đà hơn, tạo cảm giác rõ vị ngay từ những miếng đầu tiên.
Phần nhân có kích thước khá lớn. Miếng giò và chả đều đầy đặn, kết hợp với bánh dày mềm, dẻo, dính vừa phải. Với chúng tôi, hai chiếc bánh đã đủ khiến bụng no, nhất là khi phần nhân tương đối nhiều.
Tuy nhiên, vì vị giò chả đậm đà và phần ăn khá đầy đặn, món bánh có thể tạo cảm giác hơi ngấy nếu ăn liền hai chiếc mà không uống kèm nước. Đây cũng là điểm khiến trải nghiệm tại Nam Anh có phần khác với Thuỷ Hùng: hương vị nổi bật hơn về độ thơm, đậm, trong khi cảm giác ăn lại nặng vị hơn một chút.
Mức giá 20.000 đồng/cặp cao hơn Thuỷ Hùng 5.000 đồng. Với hai cặp bánh, số tiền chênh lệch là 10.000 đồng. Không phải khoản quá lớn, nhưng nếu xét riêng trải nghiệm ăn tại chỗ, Nam Anh không có lợi thế về không gian ngồi lại hay đồ uống miễn phí như địa chỉ đầu tiên.
Điểm chúng mình chấm: 8/10. Nam Anh phù hợp với những người thích bánh dày giò có mùi thơm rõ, phần nhân đậm đà và đầy đặn. Đây là lựa chọn đáng cân nhắc nếu ưu tiên hương vị và muốn mua mang đi, dù mức giá cao hơn và không gian phục vụ chủ yếu là quầy bán hàng.
3. Bánh dày giò cô Hải: Hơn 30 năm gắn bó với món quà sáng, ngồi vỉa hè ngắm phố Hà Nội
Nếu Thuỷ Hùng gây ấn tượng bởi không gian tiện nghi, Nam Anh nổi bật ở vị giò chả đậm đà thì bánh dày giò cô Hải lại mang đến cảm giác gần gũi của một hàng ăn lâu năm giữa phố Hà Nội.
Quán hiện nằm tại số 8 Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm. Theo thông tin chúng tôi ghi nhận, cô Hải đã bán bánh dày giò hơn 30 năm và từng có thời gian kinh doanh tại số 14 Nguyễn Bỉnh Khiêm, trước khi chuyển sang địa điểm mới để con gái tiếp tục bán hàng.
Không có mặt bằng rộng hay những tủ kính trưng bày đủ loại giò chả, nơi đây chỉ là một quầy hàng nhỏ đặt phía trước nhà. Bàn ghế nhựa được kê giản dị, không gian mở hoàn toàn với đường phố, không có điều hoà hay những tiện nghi như tại Thuỷ Hùng.
Thế nhưng, chính sự giản dị ấy lại tạo nên nét riêng. Khách có thể ngồi ăn bánh dày, ngắm dòng người qua lại và cảm nhận nhịp sống phố phường. Trong những ngày Hà Nội se lạnh, một món ăn nóng hổi, đơn giản bên vỉa hè đôi khi lại đem đến cảm giác dễ chịu theo cách rất riêng.
Chúng tôi gọi một cặp bánh dày giò lụa và một cặp bánh dày chả mỡ, cũng với mức giá 20.000 đồng/cặp, tổng cộng 40.000 đồng.
Bánh dày tại cô Hải mềm, dẻo và thơm, được kẹp trong lớp lá chuối. Xét về kết cấu, bánh khá giống với bánh tại Thuỷ Hùng: độ dẻo dính vừa phải, không bị cứng hay quá dai.
Với bánh dày kẹp chả mỡ, phần chả có kích thước nhỏ hơn một chút so với miếng chả tại Thuỷ Hùng. Chả có độ béo vừa phải, dễ ăn nhưng không còn cảm giác ấm nóng và mọng nước rõ rệt như chiếc bánh chúng tôi đã thử ở địa chỉ đầu tiên.
Trong khi đó, bánh dày kẹp giò lụa có phần giò khá to và dày. Hương vị nhìn chung quen thuộc, không tạo ra khác biệt quá lớn so với hai hàng còn lại. Điểm đáng chú ý nằm ở cách chuẩn bị: bánh được kéo giãn để ôm lấy miếng giò hoặc chả, giúp phần nhân được bao bọc kín hơn.
Nếu xét riêng hương vị, bánh dày cô Hải không có sự chênh lệch quá rõ rệt so với hai địa chỉ còn lại. Nhưng về không gian, đây lại là một trải nghiệm khác hẳn. Không có điều hoà, không có bàn ghế chỉn chu như một quán ăn, bù lại là cảm giác ngồi bên vỉa hè, ăn một món quà sáng truyền thống giữa phố phường Hà Nội.
Điểm chúng tôi chấm: 8/10. Cô Hải phù hợp với những người yêu thích các hàng ăn lâu năm, muốn thưởng thức bánh dày giò trong một không gian giản dị, gần gũi với nhịp sống đường phố. Nếu ưu tiên sự thoải mái, mát mẻ và nhiều tiện ích khi ngồi ăn, nơi đây sẽ không có nhiều lợi thế bằng Thuỷ Hùng.
Vậy đâu là địa chỉ đáng thử nhất khi theo trend bánh dày giò?
Sau khi trải nghiệm cả ba hàng, chúng tôi nhận thấy chất lượng bánh dày không có sự khác biệt quá lớn. Cả ba đều có phần bánh mềm, dẻo, kết hợp với giò lụa hoặc chả mỡ theo cách quen thuộc. Sự khác nhau chủ yếu nằm ở độ đậm đà của nhân, kích thước miếng giò chả, cách chuẩn bị món ăn, giá bán và không gian phục vụ.
| Địa chỉ | Giá bánh dày giò | Điểm nổi bật | Điểm chúng tôi chấm | 
| Giò chả Thuỷ Hùng | 15.000 đồng/cặp | Không gian sạch sẽ, có điều hoà, trà nhài đá miễn phí, chả mỡ ấm nóng | 10/10 | 
| Giò chả Nam Anh | Từ 20.000 đồng/cặp | Giò chả thơm, đậm vị nước mắm, phần nhân đầy đặn | 8/10 | 
| Bánh dày giò cô Hải | 20.000 đồng/cặp | Hàng bán lâu năm, không gian vỉa hè giản dị, gần gũi | 8/10 | 
Nếu chỉ xét hương vị, mỗi hàng đều có điểm đáng thử riêng. Nam Anh hợp với người thích vị giò chả đậm đà; cô Hải dành cho những ai yêu cảm giác ăn quà sáng bên vỉa hè; còn Thuỷ Hùng tạo được sự cân bằng giữa chất lượng món ăn, mức giá và trải nghiệm tại chỗ.
Với team Có Như Lời Đồn, Thuỷ Hùng là địa chỉ được yêu thích nhất trong lần trải nghiệm này. Một cặp bánh chỉ 15.000 đồng, phần giò chả vừa miệng, bánh dẻo mềm, không gian sạch sẽ, mát mẻ và còn có trà nhài đá miễn phí. Những chi tiết ấy khiến trải nghiệm trở nên trọn vẹn hơn, nhất là khi so sánh với hai địa chỉ có giá cao hơn nhưng chủ yếu phục vụ khách mua mang đi hoặc ngồi ở không gian vỉa hè.
Dù vậy, sức hút của bánh dày giò có lẽ không chỉ nằm ở chuyện tìm ra hàng nào ngon nhất. Giữa vô số món ăn mới liên tục xuất hiện trên mạng xã hội, một món quà sáng bình dân, quen thuộc từ lâu vẫn có thể khiến người trẻ tò mò, rủ nhau đi ăn và chia sẻ trải nghiệm. Đôi khi, điều khiến một món ăn trở thành xu hướng không phải sự cầu kỳ, mà chính là cảm giác thân thuộc cùng niềm vui khám phá những hương vị tưởng đã quá quen với đời sống thường ngày.

articles.title: This Anthropic proxy play is getting traders' attention – here's where they see it going
articles.text:
Who says you can't tailgate an IPO?
Traders are preparing for this week's blockbuster Anthropic IPO in different ways, including buying options on one publicly-traded fund that invests in private assets.
The Destiny Tech100 (DXYZ) is a publicly-traded, closed-end fund that invests in equity, equity-linked instruments, or shares of private funds and venture companies to gain exposure to private companies. Currently, 14% of the fund's assets are tied to Anthropic, according to the company's website.
Options volume on the fund jumped to more than 10x the 30-day average Monday, according to Cboe LiveVol data. Of the 42,300 contracts traded by midday, 41,800 were calls, with just 141 puts likely opened by buyers.
Just shy of $5.5 million in options premium on DXYZ traded on Monday, with almost all of it tied to calls, but just marginally more spent buying than selling calls, according to SpotGamma. The highest-volume contract is currently the 30-strike call expiring Friday, a 90-cent contract that needs the fund to rally 19% into the weekend to pay off.
Traders may want to be wary of how the fund traded around the SpaceX IPO: DXYZ surged almost 150% in May before unwinding all the gains in the weeks ahead of SpaceX's debut. Since then, the fund has barely moved, trading around $26.
There are other bullish signs surrounding Anthropic's IPO in the derivatives markets. Current prices for perpetual futures on the blockchain exchange Hyperliquid are implying an opening price of $98, a big pop from the $70-$78 price range quoted in the company's amended S1 filing. The AI giant is expected to price Wednesday evening and begin trading on the Nasdaq on Thursday under the ticker ANT.

articles.title: Market's Nvidia obsession obscuring an opportunity in this name
articles.text:
The market is unable to divert its attention from anything not related to the ongoing saga that is Nvidia and its embattled former CEO Jensen Huang. It's understandable, given both the detail of the story and Nvidia impact on the market. It remains the tech story du jour, and it's getting plenty of ink.
I think investors should remember there are other big names reporting this week outside of Nvidia that deserve time and attention. One such name is The Walt Disney Company (DIS).
After a prolonged period of strategic transitions, the company may finally be turning the corner. Driven by a renewed focus on the bottom line, management's cost discipline now supports a runway for double-digit earnings-per-share (EPS) gains through fiscal 2027, even as it continues to trade at about its 5-year average forward multiple of 14.3x, well below the broad market multiple of more than 18x. Trading back to a market multiple, justified if it establishes above-market EPS growth, suggests ~26% upside, which is also consistent with a sum-of-the-parts analysis that points to an intrinsic valuation of $140 to $160 per share versus the Friday, November 13th closing price of $118.97.
Disney reports Tuesday before the bell.
Despite broader macroeconomic anxieties, the theme park and cruise divisions are showing surprisingly resilient demand. Domestically, the metrics are highly encouraging: attendance is climbing, and more importantly, per-capita spending continues to rise.
On the digital front, Direct-to-Consumer (DTC) Disney's streaming margins currently sit in the low teens, respectable given the segment's previous lack of profits. But the real upside scenario requires looking ahead: if Disney can scale these DTC margins to 20% or higher, the stock could at least trade at a multiple comparable to streaming king Netflix (which would imply a share price of ~ $139 or so.
Part of the reason the studio segment remains a mixed bag is that, while there are periodic blockbuster bright spots, Disney's theatrical recovery remains uneven overall. Furthermore, legacy media continues its secular decline. The pay-TV industry has likely lost around 40 million subscribers—representing a staggering 40% erosion of the user base since 2015—and will likely lose more this year. However, the critical takeaway for investors is that the pace of cord-cutting is finally slowing down.
With linear TV stabilizing, the parks firing on all cylinders, and streaming marching toward higher profitability, Disney offers a highly asymmetric risk-reward profile. The magic is returning to Disney's financials, and the current share price heavily discounts a business fundamentally engineered for double-digit growth.
The trade
Right now, the options market is pricing a ~6% move by the end of the week (the company reports Tuesday, pre-open), which is below the 8 quarter median move of 7.4%. Anticipating a "vol crush" after earnings, I like selling December premium to help finance the purchase of a longer-dated call - a diagonal call/spread risk reversal.
When selecting an option trade consider the key things that affect its value and how those things differ from simply buying (or selling) the underlying asset. For these option trades, let's consider three sensitivities (Greeks): Delta, the rate at which the option position changes in value for changes in the underlying price. Theta, or decay, which measures how much the value of an option declines as time passes, and Vega, the change in an option's price associated with changes in the implied volatility of an option.
In the case of the diagonal risk reversal each of these factors plays into the structure to our benefit. The delta of the structure is less than 100, meaning that the p&l associated with moves up or down will be less for one spread than they would be for 100 shares of stock.
We like this because the stock has already had a decent run recently, and the option structure will lose less than the stock will if it gives that back. Because nearer dated expiration decay more rapidly as a percentage of the options value than longer dated options do (and out of the money options also exhibit accelerated decay), the shorter dated December options we're selling should decay in value more quickly than the longer dated March options we are buying, even though the March option has a higher premium. Vega can work in our favor as well due to "vol crush". When option premiums are elevated due to a catalyst such as earnings we should expect that much of that premium will be sucked out or crushed once the event has passed.
This will impact both the December and March options to a degree, but remember that the March options also capture another earnings event in February, so some measure of event variance (elevated option premium) will remain in the March expiration to account for that.

articles.title: Phát hiện 4300 gói dung dịch thuốc lá điện tử trong va li tại sân bay Đà Nẵng
articles.text:
Phát hiện 4300 gói dung dịch thuốc lá điện tử trong va li tại sân bay Đà Nẵng
Ngày 17/11, Cục Hải quan cho hay, Hải quan cửa khẩu sân bay quốc tế Đà Nẵng vừa phát hiện 424 cây nghi là thuốc lá nung nóng và 4.300 gói dung dịch dùng cho thuốc lá điện tử trong hành lý của hai hành khách nhập cảnh từ Hàn Quốc.
- 17-11-2026Hai điểm đến Việt Nam vào danh sách những nơi đáng trải nghiệm nhất châu Á
- 16-11-2026Phó Thủ tướng Phạm Thị Thanh Trà: Chọn 5 địa phương làm điểm phát triển kinh tế bạc
- 16-11-2026Triệu tập 86 người liên quan hệ thống BIT99: Nhiều người trẻ, sinh viên tìm việc làm bị dụ bán nhà, vay nợ để đầu tư
- 03-10-20264 người trong một gia đình cùng bị khởi tố, công an thu giữ gần 9000 gói thuốc lá nhập lậu
- 16-06-2026Bán thuốc lá nhập lậu, chủ cửa hàng tạp hóa bị khởi tố
Ngày 8/11, khi làm thủ tục cho chuyến bay từ Incheon (Hàn Quốc) đến Đà Nẵng, Hải quan cửa khẩu sân bay quốc tế Đà Nẵng phát hiện dấu hiệu nghi vấn trong hành lý của hai hành khách quốc tịch Hàn Quốc.
Lực lượng chức năng kiểm tra 6 vali của hai hành khách này. Kết quả kiểm đếm cho thấy 424 cây nói trên gồm 4.240 bao sản phẩm mang các nhãn hiệu Terea, Miix, Fiit và Aiim. Ngoài số sản phẩm đóng bao và các gói dung dịch, lực lượng chức năng còn phát hiện 4 thiết bị điện tử.
Hai hành khách không khai báo hải quan đối với số hàng này và không có hóa đơn, chứng từ kèm theo. Theo lời khai ban đầu của hai hành khách, số hàng được mang vào Việt Nam để tiêu thụ.
Hải quan cửa khẩu sân bay quốc tế Đà Nẵng đã lập hồ sơ, tạm giữ toàn bộ số hàng và chuyển giao vụ việc cho cơ quan chức năng. Cơ quan Cảnh sát điều tra Công an thành phố Đà Nẵng đã ban hành quyết định khởi tố liên quan đến vụ việc.
Cục Hải quan cho biết thêm, Việt Nam cấm nhập khẩu, vận chuyển và sử dụng thuốc lá điện tử, thuốc lá nung nóng từ năm 2025 theo Nghị quyết số 173/2024/QH15 của Quốc hội. Hai mặt hàng này thuộc danh mục hàng hóa cấm nhập khẩu tại Phụ lục I ban hành kèm theo Nghị định số 292/2026/NĐ-CP ngày 22/7/2026 của Chính phủ. Vì vậy, hành khách không được mang các sản phẩm này vào Việt Nam, kể cả để sử dụng cá nhân.
Đối với sản phẩm dạng dung dịch, Nghị định số 371/2025/NĐ-CP của Chính phủ quy định dung dịch thuốc lá điện tử có thể chứa hoặc không chứa nicotine. Vì vậy, hành khách không thể chỉ căn cứ vào dòng chữ “không chứa nicotine” trên bao bì để xác định sản phẩm được phép mang vào Việt Nam.

articles.title: Một doanh nghiệp 12.000 lao động sắp “phát” gần 500 tỷ đồng trả cổ tức, một CTCK bỏ túi hàng chục tỷ
articles.text:
Một doanh nghiệp 12.000 lao động sắp “phát” gần 500 tỷ đồng trả cổ tức, một CTCK bỏ túi hàng chục tỷ
Với tỷ lệ cổ tức 40%, một công ty chứng khoán cũng dự kiến thu về hàng chục tỷ đồng từ đợt chi trả này.
Tổng công ty Lưu ký và Bù trừ chứng khoán Việt Nam (VSDC) vừa thông báo ngày 27/11 tới đây sẽ là ngày đăng ký cuối cùng để CTCP May Sông Hồng (mã chứng khoán: MSH) thực hiện tạm ứng cổ tức năm 2026 bằng tiền mặt.
Tỷ lệ thực hiện là 40%, tương ứng cổ đông sở hữu mỗi cổ phiếu sẽ được nhận 4.000 đồng. Với hơn 112,5 triệu cổ phiếu đang lưu hành, May Sông Hồng dự kiến chi hơn 450 tỷ đồng cho đợt trả cổ tức lần này. Thời gian thanh toán vào ngày 19/1/2027, trước kỳ nghỉ Tết Nguyên đán.
Theo báo cáo tài chính hợp nhất quý 3/2026, ông Bùi Đức Thịnh, Chủ tịch HĐQT May Sông Hồng, là cổ đông lớn nhất tại doanh nghiệp với hơn 26,9 triệu cổ phiếu, tương ứng 23,91% vốn điều lệ. Nếu giữ nguyên lượng sở hữu đến ngày chốt quyền, ông Thịnh dự kiến nhận về khoảng 108 tỷ đồng cổ tức.
Trong khi đó, ông Bùi Việt Quang, Phó Chủ tịch Thường trực HĐQT kiêm Phó Tổng Giám đốc, và bà Bùi Thu Hà, Thành viên HĐQT, dự kiến lần lượt nhận về hơn 51 tỷ đồng và gần 35 tỷ đồng.
Đáng chú ý, CTCP Chứng khoán FPT (FPTS, mã FTS) cũng là cổ đông lớn của May Sông Hồng. Tại thời điểm cuối tháng 9/2026, công ty chứng khoán này nắm giữ 12 triệu cổ phiếu MSH, tương ứng 10,66% vốn điều lệ. Với lượng sở hữu trên, FPTS dự kiến thu về 48 tỷ đồng tiền cổ tức.
May Sông Hồng là một trong những doanh nghiệp dệt may duy trì chính sách trả cổ tức tiền mặt tỷ lệ cao trên sàn chứng khoán. Trong năm 2025, doanh nghiệp thực hiện chia cổ tức bằng tiền với tổng tỷ lệ 50%, tương ứng 5.000 đồng/cổ phiếu. Kế hoạch cổ tức năm 2026 được ĐHĐCĐ thông qua ở mức 40-50%.
Trên thị trường chứng khoán, kết phiên giao dịch ngày 16/11, cổ phiếu MSH có giá 34.500 đồng/cổ phiếu, tương ứng vốn hóa thị trường hơn 3.880 tỷ đồng.
Về kết quả kinh doanh, trong quý 3/2026, May Sông Hồng ghi nhận doanh thu thuần đạt 1.630 tỷ đồng, giảm khoảng 1% so với cùng kỳ năm trước. Tuy nhiên, nhờ giá vốn giảm nhanh hơn doanh thu, lợi nhuận gộp vẫn tăng 4,2% lên hơn 364 tỷ đồng, đưa biên lợi nhuận gộp từ 21,2% lên 22,3%.
Ở chiều ngược lại, doanh thu hoạt động tài chính giảm hơn 33% xuống còn gần 38 tỷ đồng, trong khi chi phí tài chính và chi phí quản lý doanh nghiệp đều tăng. Kết quả, May Sông Hồng báo lợi nhuận sau thuế hợp nhất quý 3 đạt hơn 196 tỷ đồng, giảm 2,2% so với cùng kỳ.
Lũy kế 9 tháng đầu năm 2026, doanh nghiệp ghi nhận doanh thu thuần đạt 4.329 tỷ đồng và lợi nhuận trước thuế đạt 577 tỷ đồng, lần lượt tăng 4,3% và 0,9% so với cùng kỳ. Lợi nhuận sau thuế hợp nhất đạt gần 481 tỷ đồng, tăng 2,8%, trong đó lợi nhuận thuộc về cổ đông công ty mẹ đạt gần 416 tỷ đồng.
So với mục tiêu lợi nhuận trước thuế 900 tỷ đồng được ĐHĐCĐ thông qua, May Sông Hồng đã thực hiện được hơn 64% kế hoạch cả năm sau 9 tháng.
Tại thời điểm 30/9/2026, tổng tài sản của May Sông Hồng đạt hơn 4.930 tỷ đồng, tăng 5,4% so với đầu năm. Doanh nghiệp và các công ty con có tổng cộng 11.610 lao động.
